# SK2092 — `NullReferenceException` is caught

<!-- Generated from Rules/Rikarin.Skala.Rules.Metadata/rules.json. Do not edit. -->

A `catch` clause names `NullReferenceException` as the type it handles.

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | Correctness |
| Default severity | warning |
| Scope | Syntax |
| Needs a compilation | no |
| Fix | no |
| Language version floor | — |
| Since | 2.0 |
| Supersedes | S1696 |

## Why

A `NullReferenceException` is a dereference that should not have happened, and naming it in a `catch` converts that bug into a control-flow path the program is expected to take. The handler also covers a region far larger than the one dereference that was meant, so the next null anywhere under the `try` is silently absorbed by a recovery written for a different one. The repair is a null check at the dereference, not a handler around the region.

## Example

Instead of:

```csharp
try {
    Render(model.Header);
} catch (NullReferenceException) {
    Render(Fallback);
}
```

Write:

```csharp
if (model.Header is null) {
    Render(Fallback);
} else {
    Render(model.Header);
}
```

## When it does not fire

⚠ **`catch (Exception)` catches it too and is deliberately not this rule.** A catch-all is a different decision with a different argument — sometimes a correct one at a process boundary — and folding the two together would make the finding unanswerable. The rule fires only where `NullReferenceException` is the type the clause itself names, which is the author stating that a null dereference is an expected outcome; a bare `catch`, a `catch (SystemException)` and a `catch (ArgumentNullException)` are all silent. ⚠ **Syntactic, matching the name as written**, in the three spellings a compiling program can use. The residual is a user-defined type whose own simple name is `NullReferenceException`, or a `using` alias for the framework one; neither occurs on either reference tree or anywhere in `Testing/corpus`, and buying them would cost the rule its ability to run under `--load=loose`, which is where most of the code an agent writes is first seen. Report-only: the repair is a null check somewhere under the `try` and not at the `catch`, no edit here can write it, and deleting the clause would turn a swallowed bug into a crash without anyone deciding that.
